admission.workflow: Present one statically admitted Candidate browser item while privileged Electron code enforces a revision-frozen navigation policy and protects minimized ordered activity.

items.rationale: Canonical Microsoft MIT text for the reviewed browser evidence.
Retain a single active browser lifecycle, reuse boundary and explicit disposal under an Attempt-scoped privileged coordinator rather than an extension-owned webview.
Its arbitrary iframe source, scripts/forms/downloads, external-open action, extension settings and URL restoration conflict with the privileged revision-frozen Candidate browser boundary.
The Candidate pane owns native WebContentsView bounds, visibility, overlay blocking, focus, isolated zoom conversion and teardown through a closed validated renderer-to-main surface protocol.
A generic webview service and arbitrary extension content/protocol lifecycle are broader than the one closed Candidate browser capability.

dependencies.rationale: Only the static Candidate composition admits the browser item type and contribution.
The pinned Electron WebContentsView/session boundary performs privileged request and navigation enforcement.
The Exam Security Coordinator supplies current Attempt, Participation and posture gates through the closed gate projection.

divergences.summary: Exact ASCII HTTP(S) origins, normalized path prefixes, explicit subdomains/redirects/HTTP exceptions and immutable correction ordinals replace arbitrary URL and iframe behavior.

A dedicated sandboxed WebContentsView/session denies popups, permissions, downloads, DevTools, external schemes and unlisted subresources; renderer preload exposes only validated projection, intents, events and native-surface updates.

The active Candidate pane publishes exact viewport geometry and visibility; Electron validates sender and shape, converts CSS pixels with the owning renderer zoom, clamps to CandidateWindow content bounds, and keeps the native view hidden while blocked, overlaid, switched, zero-sized, or closing. Separate canOpen and canClose capabilities preserve underlying native ownership while policy gates presentation.

Only five top-level/lifecycle kinds enter a bounded protected source-sequenced ledger with exact sequence-or-gap coverage and bounded deduplicated acknowledgement requests; policy correction seals the old revision/digest scope before rebinding, renderer projections are exact and state-consistent, and queries, fragments, credentials, headers, content, cookies and subresources cannot enter records.

verification.obligation: Verify canonicalization, wildcard/path/redirect/HTTP exception decisions, unsafe form rejection, activity minimization, protected exact sequence/replay/ack/gap behavior, policy-scope rotation and gate transitions.

Verify pane-owned native surface bounds, overlay and item-switch hiding, focus transfer, blocked assignment reopening, blocked native-owner closure, close-failure propagation, and responsive toolbar/sidebar behavior in real Chromium at 200% zoom.

Verify the real sandboxed Electron WebContentsView receives its bounded visible surface and denies popup, permission, redirect target, prohibited subresource, sensitive-scheme recording and DevTools behavior.
Verify runtime placement, layer direction, static Candidate composition, preload closure and cycle absence.
Verify reviewed Simple Browser, WebContentsView and webview-service evidence at the exact pinned VS Code revision.
